1.1.1.174.rationale: 2-hydroxycyclohexan-1-one:NAD+ oxidoreductase is an obscure single-activity dehydrogenase; literature search for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context returned zero hits.

1.1.1.179.rationale: D-xylose:NADP+ 1-oxidoreductase (xylose reductase) shows no credible evidence of a fused second catalytic activity; the single hit found concerned an unrelated short-chain dehydrogenase (SalM).
1.1.1.179.evidence: PMID 20736169 (unrelated enzyme, not supporting bifunctionality); otherwise none found, defaulted to monofunctional

1.1.1.18.rationale: myo-Inositol:NAD+ 2-oxidoreductase (inositol dehydrogenase) search hits were unrelated genomics/metagenomics papers; no description of a fused second catalytic domain was found.

1.1.1.188.rationale: This prostaglandin-related NADP-oxidoreductase overlaps with aldo-keto reductase family members (e.g., AKR1B3) that show broad substrate promiscuity (acting as PGF2alpha synthase), but this is substrate promiscuity of one catalytic mechanism, not a second fused catalytic activity.
1.1.1.188.evidence: PMID 20093363 (substrate promiscuity, not a fused second activity)

1.1.1.19.rationale: L-Gulonate:NADP+ 6-oxidoreductase has no literature indicating a second fused catalytic activity; the only hit found was an unrelated moth pheromone transcriptome study.

1.1.1.2.rationale: EC 1.1.1.2 (NADP-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase) is predominantly a single-activity oxidoreductase; the classic bifunctional aldehyde/alcohol dehydrogenase fusions (AdhE-type, e.g. a rare hyperthermophilic Fe-ADH) are atypical exceptions generally associated with NAD-dependent EC 1.1.1.1/1.2.1.10 activity rather than the defining behavior of this EC.
1.1.1.2.evidence: PMID 33441766 describes an atypical bifunctional Fe-ADH but is not representative of EC 1.1.1.2 generally; defaulted to monofunctional

1.1.1.200.rationale: D-Sorbitol 6-phosphate:NADP+ 1-oxidoreductase returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context, consistent with a simple single-activity dehydrogenase.

1.1.1.215.rationale: 5-dehydro-D-gluconate:NADP+ 2-oxidoreductase returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.221.rationale: This obscure plant oxidoreductase (ionol-related) returned zero literature hits suggesting a second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.1.227.rationale: (-)-Borneol:NAD+ oxidoreductase (borneol dehydrogenase) returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.234.rationale: (2S)-Flavan-4-ol:NADP+ 4-oxidoreductase hits were unrelated plant stress/transcriptomics studies; no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity was found.

1.1.1.240.rationale: N-Acetyl-D-glucosamine:NAD+ 1-oxidoreductase returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.251.rationale: Galactitol-1-phosphate:NAD+ oxidoreductase had only one unrelated hit (E. coli chemostat flux study); no evidence of a second fused catalytic activity.

1.1.1.274.rationale: 2-dehydro-D-gluconate:NADP+ 2-oxidoreductase hits were unrelated (EC annotation ambiguity commentary, Salmonella comparative genomics); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.282.rationale: Literature explicitly distinguishes this NADPH-specific shikimate dehydrogenase (AroE) as catalyzing only the single reduction of 3-dehydroshikimate to shikimate, contrasted against the separate paralogous protein YdiB (quinate/shikimate dehydrogenase, not this EC) that is broadly substrate-promiscuous; AroE itself carries no second fused catalytic activity.
1.1.1.282.evidence: PMID 15735308; PMID 12837789 (both confirm AroE is single-activity, contrasted with the distinct YdiB protein)

1.1.1.284.rationale: S-(hydroxymethyl)glutathione dehydrogenase (glutathione-dependent formaldehyde dehydrogenase / class III ADH) uses one catalytic mechanism across related thiol-adduct substrates (including S-nitrosoglutathione reduction); this is substrate promiscuity, not a second distinct EC-type catalytic activity. No fusion evidence found in search hits (unrelated thiol biology/microbiome papers).

1.1.1.287.rationale: D-arabinitol:NADP+ oxidoreductase returned zero literature hits for bifunctional/multifunctional/trifunctional context.

1.1.1.31.rationale: 3-Hydroxy-2-methylpropanoate:NAD+ oxidoreductase (3-hydroxyisobutyrate dehydrogenase) hits concerned a related but distinct enzyme (ketol-acid reductoisomerase) in the same structural superfamily, not a fused second catalytic activity in this enzyme itself.

1.1.1.312.rationale: This obscure dehydrogenase (5-carboxymethyl-2-hydroxymuconic-semialdehyde:NAD+ oxidoreductase) had only one unrelated hit (soil pollution microbiome study); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.314.rationale: This obscure KEGG-reaction-named oxidoreductase had only one unrelated hit (seaweed terpenome gene survey); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.

1.1.1.4.rationale: (R,R)-Butane-2,3-diol:NAD+ oxidoreductase (butanediol dehydrogenase) literature focuses on substrate/stereo-specificity of a single catalytic activity (acetoin/2,3-butanediol interconversion); no fused second catalytic activity described.
1.1.1.4.evidence: PMID 37644496 (substrate specificity of single activity, not bifunctionality)

1.1.1.44.rationale: 6-phospho-D-gluconate:NADP+ 2-oxidoreductase (decarboxylating) is a well-characterized single concerted oxidative-decarboxylation activity; despite many hits, none described a genuine fused second catalytic activity (most were unrelated genomics/annotation papers).

1.1.1.49.rationale: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) is extensively studied as a single-activity oxidoreductase (first step of pentose phosphate pathway); search hits (including a dedicated structural review) describe no fused second catalytic domain.
1.1.1.49.evidence: PMID 39259139 (structural review, describes single activity, no fusion)

1.1.1.79.rationale: Glycolate/glyoxylate:NADP+ oxidoreductase hits were unrelated pathway reviews (serine biosynthesis branches, TCA anaplerosis); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity. Known broad substrate range (glyoxylate/hydroxypyruvate) reflects promiscuity of one mechanism, not two fused EC activities.

1.1.1.87.rationale: Homoisocitrate dehydrogenase (decarboxylating) had only one unrelated hit (Euglena metabolic pathway review); no evidence of a fused second catalytic activity.
